messages:
michael_cust: Hey — we're getting a 400 from /v1/embeddings after switching to batch. Error message: "embedding dimensions mismatch (expected 1536, got 1537)". This started when we changed our client to send batches. Example curl we used:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"input":"[0.12,0.34,0.56,...]"}'

Any pointers?

alex_support: Thanks — can you paste the exact request body (not redacted) and the X-Request-ID from the response headers if you have it? Also: are you sending already-computed numeric vectors, or raw text that you want the API to embed?

michael_cust: We're sending precomputed vectors (numpy arrays) from the client. In our JS we ended up doing: body = JSON.stringify({ input: JSON.stringify(vec) }) because the client wrapper was failing on a raw array. So the request body actually looks like: '{"input":"[0.1,0.2,0.3,...]"}'. We get mixed dims across items in the batch — some 1536, some 1537 — super confusing.

jess_dev: That pattern explains it. Two issues likely: 1) You're double-stringifying the vector, so the server sees a string (the JSON text) and will compute an embedding of that string rather than accept a precomputed vector. 2) If some items are nested differently (e.g., [[...]] vs [...]) the batch parser can treat elements inconsistently leading to perceived dimension mismatches.

Correct usage examples:

- If you want the API to compute embeddings from text (batch):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "input": ["hello world", "second item"]
}
```

- If you are trying to upload precomputed vectors for storage/indexing, do NOT send them to the embeddings generation endpoint as the service expects text input there. Use the vectors/upsert endpoint (or your index API). Example pseudo-upsert payload (your index service):
```
POST /v1/index/upsert
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "vectors": [
    {"id": "doc1", "values": [0.12, 0.34, ...]},
    {"id": "doc2", "values": [0.23, 0.45, ...]}
  ]
}
```

Also, check your client code: if you do axios.post(url, JSON.stringify(payload)) you may be double-encoding. Instead do axios.post(url, payload) with Content-Type: application/json so axios handles serialization.

alex_support: Also note: if your client accidentally sends Content-Type: text/plain (some runtimes do when body is a string) the server will parse the whole body as a string. That produces exactly the behaviour you saw.

michael_cust: Ahhh okay makes sense. We were stringifying because the firebase function was complaining when we passed a raw JS array through their messaging layer. We'll change to pass a native array to the upsert endpoint. Question: we also saw intermittent 413 when trying to upsert ~10k vectors in one request — any throughput tips?

tara_eng: For large upserts, chunk on the client. Start with 500 vectors per request and tune up/down based on observed latency and memory. If your vectors are high-dim (>=1536) reduce batch size. Use exponential backoff on 413/429 and monitor request size; gzip helps but some endpoints limit uncompressed payloads.

jess_dev: One more debug trick: if you want to confirm what the server received, enable request logging on your client or add a logging proxy (ngrok/localdev) and inspect the raw HTTP body. That quickly shows if you double-stringified or if there are extra escape characters/newlines.

alex_support: LMK when you have a small repro (2 items) and the X-Request-ID and we'll pull logs. Glad this narrowed it down. :thumbsup:

michael_cust: Thanks — I'll try sending arrays to the upsert API and test chunking. Will post a mini repro here if still broken. Appreciate the quick triage.
